title: How to Protect Margins from FX Risk Using Budget Rates and Hedging
summary: How to Protect Margins from FX Risk Using Budget Rates and Hedging
body_text: How to Protect Margins from FX Risk Using Budget Rates and Hedging Why Budgeting Is the Foundation of FX Risk Management How to Measure FX Rate Variance: Budget vs. Actual Analysis What Is Constant Currency Reporting? What Is FX Rate Variance? FX Variance Formula: How to Calculate FX Impact Managing FX Risk Through Hedging Strategies FAQs How to Protect Margins from FX Risk Using Budget Rates and Hedging Although accrual accounting has been the standard since the Italian Renaissance , its application can miss the impact of foreign exchange (FX) movements have on financial performance, and, and like life, it all comes down to timing. Revenue and expense recognition criteria dictate when forecasted transactions are recorded on financial statements. That means the impact FX movements have also doesn’t ‘show up’ on financial statements until these recognition criteria are met. In practice , FX risk can impact margins and cash flow long before it appears in financial statements. Earlier, we explored how FX flows through and is captured on financial statements . Following the process chronologically, much of the impact FX movements have on a business's financial performance happens before the first invoice, purchase order, and corresponding asset or liability are recorded. This early-stage exposure is often referred to as forecast FX exposure or budget FX risk. If this is the case , how do finance departments and FP&A teams identify and visualize the materiality of this FX risk? Why Budgeting Is the Foundation of FX Risk Management The budget is the baseline . Until something is recorded, it can’t be measured —and when transactions are recorded, or recognized, they are governed by the accounting standards applied. That being said, currency movements affecting future sales, costs, or cash flows don't typically trigger accounting entries until a transaction occurs. Fundamentally, an FX exposure is not going to be captured in financial statements until after an expense or revenue in foreign currency is recognized. This creates a gap between economic FX exposure and accounting recognition. In fact, without a budgeting process that includes explicit FX budget rates, there is no way to capture margin erosion from FX or cash flow volatility. It simply results in lower revenue, higher expenses, and less predictable cash flows. Nearly every year I encounter businesses with nine-figure toplines and seven-figure margin erosion from FX movements. These businesses simply did not know how much FX exposure they had in their business and how badly it impacted them, other than having a vague understanding that they didn't do as well as they wanted to because their FX exposure was not properly measured through budget assumptions. This is why budgeting and cash forecasts that contain explicit FX budget rates are essential for finance teams. It creates the yardstick to decompose variances driven from FX movements versus other factors. Budget FX rates serve as the benchmark for measuring FX rate variance and protecting operating margins. As shown below, decomposing budgets versus actuals generates powerful insights in highlighting the factors that drive a business’ financial performance. FX rates are one of these factors. Source: ExpertsMInd.com: Relationship among variances, Cost Accounting How to Measure FX Rate Variance: Budget vs. Actual Analysis Going back to Managerial Accounting 101 , we know that many FP&A teams apply a Price-Volume-Mix decomposition of their variance-to-actual to capture the variables that are impacting their financial performance. FX rates are simply another component of this process, which is why setting budget FX rates, as outlined in the earlier piece, is a critical component of effective FX risk management. Once those budgeted rates are applied to budgets and cash forecasts, FP&A teams can apply the below. What Is Constant Currency Reporting? Constant Currency Reporting records the actual results using the budgeted FX rate. This reveals how the business performed operationally (e.g., did we sell more units?). Constant currency analysis removes FX volatility to isolate true operational performance. This shows what results would have been had FX movements not occurred: the ‘true’ operational performance of the business. What Is FX Rate Variance? FX Rate Variance compares actual results at actual rates versus actual results at budgeted rates. This isolates the exact amount that currency volatility reduced or boosted your margins. This calculation directly quantifies the financial impact of foreign exchange risk on profitability . This is simply the realized result. You can extract this information directly from your accounting/ERP system and compare it to the budget results. Applying the same process to cash forecasts to assess their accuracy will also reveal how FX movements can impact the volatility of cash flow. This is particularly important for treasury teams managing liquidity risk and debt obligations, especially in heavily levered firms or those in workout situations. FX Variance Formula: How to Calculate FX Impact The variance formula is quite simple in both instances: FX Impact = (Actual Rate − Budget Rate) × Foreign Currency Amount This formula provides a direct measurement of how exchange rate movements impact margins, revenue, and cash flow. Managing FX Risk Through Hedging Strategies As highlighted earlier, spot FX rates can be quite volatile , and even developed market currencies can expect high single-digit annual movements. This math is unforgiving. FX variances can easily be much larger than other variance drivers that can result in unemployment for the managers involved. While explicitly including FX rates in the budgeting process will help businesses uncover the source and materiality of FX risk in their business, it is not a panacea. Budgeting allows businesses to measure FX risk, but the exposure itself remains. Hedging is the primary tool used to actively manage and reduce that risk. So what is there to do? Stay tuned. In our next piece, we will show how the budgeting process above integrates into the development of cash flow hedging programs. These hedging strategies allow treasury teams to protect margins, stabilize cash flow, and reduce earnings volatility caused by FX movements. Additional Resources: Subscribe to our Market Commentary Explore our Currency Research site Book a Meeting with Sean FAQs What is accrual accounting? Accrual accounting is the recognition of an expense or revenue and corresponding balance sheet item at the time it is incurred – not when cash changes hands. The most common example is the recognition of revenue from a sale, with payment terms, while cash has not been received from the sale. The sale is recognized on the income statement but because cash has not been received from the sale a corresponding accounts receivable asset is created. The subsequent receipt of cash reduces the accounts receivable balance while cash increases. Both items are working capital items which are subject to remeasurement, in future periods, to account for how changes in FX rates effect their valuation, if these items are denominated in a different currency, then the reporting currency of the accounts. The challenge accrual accounting presents for FX risk is that the impact FX rate variations have on forecasted transactions is not recorded because those transactions are not recognized until they occur. What is FX risk in budgeting? FX risk in budgeting is the potential for exchange rate movements to cause actual revenue, expenses, and margins to differ from planned budget assumptions. When companies set budgets using specific FX rates, any deviation from those rates creates variances that directly impact financial performance. What is constant currency reporting? Constant currency reporting is a method that measures financial performance using budgeted or prior-period exchange rates instead of actual rates. This isolates operational performance by removing the impact of currency volatility. How do FP&A teams measure FX impact? FP&A teams measure FX impact by comparing actual financial results at budget rates versus actual exchange rates. This process isolates FX rate variance and separates currency effects from operational performance. How can companies protect margins from FX risk? Companies protect margins from FX risk by identifying exposures in budgets and implementing hedging strategies such as forwards or cash flow hedges. These tools help stabilize cash flow and reduce earnings volatility. What is the formula to calculate FX impact? The formula to calculate FX impact is (Actual Rate – Budget Rate) × Foreign Currency Amount. This calculation shows the direct financial effect of exchange rate changes. What is forecast FX exposure? Forecast FX exposure, also called budget FX risk, is the potential impact of exchange rate movements on future revenues, costs, or cash flows that have not yet been recorded as accounting transactions. It is measured through the budgeting process using explicit FX budget rates. Sean Coakley, CFA Director, Strategic Sales & Market Strategist Sean works with corporate clients and institutional investors focusing on financial risk management, international treasury and working capital optimization. title: From Horseback to Real-Time Observability
summary: When America’s founders declared independence in 1776, communication traveled at the speed of a horse.
body_text: When America’s founders declared independence in 1776, communication traveled at the speed of a horse. Messages moved between colonies via riders, ships, and handwritten letters. Information that today can be transmitted across the country in milliseconds often took days or weeks to arrive. As the nation celebrates its 250th anniversary, the contrast is extraordinary. The founders could never have imagined a world of cloud computing, video collaboration, mobile devices, and digital government services. Yet they would undoubtedly recognize the importance of effective communication in accomplishing the job of serving citizens effectively. For federal civilian agencies , effective communications increasingly depends on technology. Employees collaborate across regional offices, field locations, and remote facilities . Citizens expect government services to be available whenever and wherever they need them. Digital experiences have become a primary channel through which agencies deliver value to the public. The challenge is ensuring that these experiences perform reliably across an increasingly distributed environment. Supporting the Modern Federal Workforce Today’s federal employees have access to capabilities that previous generations could scarcely imagine. Teams in 2026 may be separated by hundreds or thousands of miles and yet can collaborate instantly. Critical applications and data are accessible from virtually anywhere. Decisions that once required extensive coordination over weeks and months can now be made in real time. These advances have transformed how agencies operate, but they have also created new dependencies. Productivity relies on the performance of networks , applications, cloud services , and collaboration tools. Delays can ripple across teams, impacting operations and reducing employee efficiency. A slow application . A dropped video conference . An intermittent network issue at a remote location. Individually, these incidents may seem minor. Collectively, they can affect individual services, project execution, employee efficiency, and operational effectiveness. For example, imagine issues with application services supporting passport renewals or uploading tax returns that can have a significant impact on U.S. citizens. This is where observability has become a strategic advantage rather than simply an IT function. By providing end-to-end visibility across infrastructure, applications, and digital services, observability enables agencies to quickly identify performance issues, understand their root causes, and resolve them before they disrupt operations. Rather than reacting to problems after employees submit help desk tickets, IT teams can proactively identify issues as they emerge in their digital environments and resolve the performance issue before users are impacted. The result is a more resilient digital infrastructure that enables government employees to focus on serving the public rather than troubleshooting technology. Connecting a Distributed Nation The federal government’s footprint extends far beyond Washington, D.C. Agencies operate regional offices, service centers, laboratories, field facilities, court houses, federal reserve banks, and other remote locations across the country. Unlike the colonial era, when physical distance created unavoidable communication delays, modern technology enables agencies to function as connected enterprises. Subject matter experts can support operations nationwide. Teams can collaborate across locations in real time. Information can be shared instantly among stakeholders. But seamless communication depends on seamless performance. As agencies continue adopting cloud-based applications, unified communications platforms, and hybrid work models, maintaining visibility into user experiences becomes increasingly complex. Traditional monitoring approaches often leave blind spots, particularly at remote locations where local issues can be difficult to identify and diagnose. Comprehensive observability helps close those gaps. With actionable insights into service performance and user experience, agencies can ensure employees remain connected to the tools and information they need, regardless of location. This visibility helps maintain operational continuity while supporting the flexibility and agility that a modern government requires . Delivering Better Experiences for Citizens Perhaps nowhere has digital transformation had a greater impact than in the relationship between government agencies and the citizens they serve . Services that once required multiple office visits, mailed forms, and lengthy processing times are increasingly delivered through digital channels. Citizens expect fast, reliable, and intuitive interactions, whether they are accessing information, applying for benefits, submitting documentation, or engaging with agency personnel. Every digital interaction influences public trust. When services perform well, agencies improve accessibility, responsiveness, and citizen satisfaction. When systems are slow or unavailable, the effects extend beyond technology metrics. They directly affect the public’s experience with government. Observability provides agencies with a clearer understanding of those experiences. By monitoring service delivery from the user’s perspective, agencies can identify emerging issues, optimize performance, and ensure that digital services meet growing expectations. The ability to proactively address performance challenges helps create a more consistent and reliable experience for citizens. Building the Foundation for the Future As America celebrates its 250th year, federal agencies continue to modernize how they serve the nation. Technology may be dramatically different from anything imagined in 1776, but the goals remain familiar: communicate effectively, make informed decisions, and deliver services that improve the lives of citizens. Achieving those goals in today’s distributed digital environment requires visibility, insight, and resilience. Observability is strategic in helping to provide all three. By enabling agencies to maintain productivity, support seamless communications, and enhance citizen experiences, it strengthens the digital foundation upon which modern government depends. The means of communication have evolved from horseback messengers to real-time digital services. And NETSCOUT observability is enabling three critical objectives for federal leaders: Workforce productivity wherever they perform their jobs Reliable communications across a distributed government Better digital experiences for American citizens Learn how one federal civilian agency improved visibility and operational performance across remote locations in this related case study on overcoming observability challenges in distributed environments.

title: How a Gen Z Fashion Startup Extracted 350,000+ E-Commerce Products with Reworkd
body_text: About Lookbk Lookbk is a fashion startup where users text its AI-powered phone number outfit inspiration, such as social media screenshots, to specific requests like "Find me a red Ralph Lauren sweater, size medium," and receive curated product recommendations instantly. By eliminating friction between inspiration and purchase, they make it 10 times faster for users to find and buy the fashion they love. The Challenge “As an early-stage startup, building and maintaining scrapers in-house consumed too much time. With plans to scale up considerably in the coming months, our manual approach to data collection just wasn’t sustainable.” — Caelin Sutch, Co-founder of Lookbk Lookbk needed to gather extensive product data from many curated e-commerce sites, all mapped to its own internal schema. They initially used a headless browser service to avoid managing headless browsers themselves while still writing Playwright code for each site manually. However, this approach still had several key issues: Scraper Maintenance: E-commerce sites frequently changed layouts, breaking scrapers and forcing their engineers to drop everything to fix it - diverting attention from the core platform. Scalability Concerns: With plans to increase scraper coverage by 10×, the current process simply wouldn’t work. Bot Detection: Standard residential proxies weren’t enough to bypass anti-bot measures on many sites. Why Reworkd Recognizing that ongoing scraper maintenance would hamper long-term growth, Lookbk began searching for a platform that could resolve these challenges. Reworkd solves Lookbk’s immediate scraping maintenance issues and can easily enable them to scale to 10× more sites in the future by using LLMs to dynamically generate and maintain Playwright scraping code. Combined with Reworkd’s fully managed solution, Lookbk no longer has to spend any time on data extraction and can simply let Reworkd keep the pipeline running smoothly—no matter how often websites change. "Before Reworkd, we spent countless frustrating hours fixing scrapers every time a site changed—now it’s automated. Their advanced captcha solving also unlocks data from sites we couldn’t access before. Scaling our data pipeline is suddenly no longer an issue." Caelin Sutch Co-founder of Lookbk The Result Zero Maintenance Overhead Reduced 40 hours/month of engineering time to 0 , resulting in a 30% reduction in data extraction costs. Access to More Sites 20% more sites are now accessible (previously blocked by bot detection), giving customers access to a broader range of sources. Expanded data coverage without the need to hire additional engineers or manage proxies. Rapid Implementation Timeline to scrape new sites reduced to days - not weeks . Scraped 350K products and over 1M product images . Dedicated Slack Support Larger issues are resolved in hours , not days—minimizing disruption to data flows. title: PPL Electric Utilities restores power to more than 245,000 customers
summary: ALLENTOWN, Pa. (July 7, 2026) – PPL Electric Utilities’ crews continue to make strong progress restoring service following multiple rounds of severe weather that moved through the company's...
body_text: ALLENTOWN, Pa. (July 7, 2026) – PPL Electric Utilities’ crews continue to make strong progress restoring service following multiple rounds of severe weather that moved through the company's service territory over the Fourth of July holiday weekend. Since restoration efforts began, more than 245,000 customers have had their power restored. As of Monday night, service had been restored to more than 85% of customers affected by the storms, and the company remains on track to restore customers within timeframes shared and is ahead of schedule to restore service to at least 95% of impacted customers by 11 p.m. tonight, with nearly all remaining customers restored by 11 p.m. Wednesday, July 8. More than 264,000 customers experienced outages during this series of storms, making it one of the most impactful storm events in PPL Electric's history. “We know every remaining outage represents a customer, family or business waiting to get back to normal,” said Christine Martin, President of PPL Electric Utilities. “While we've restored service to the vast majority of customers affected by these storms, our work isn't finished. We're continuing to deploy every available resource to restore power safely to those who remain without service as quickly as possible." Largest Workforce Since Hurricane Sandy More than 3,000 personnel are currently supporting restoration efforts across PPL Electric's service territory, including company line workers, contractors, forestry crews, damage assessors and mutual assistance personnel from neighboring utilities. This is the largest restoration workforce PPL Electric has assembled since Hurricane Sandy in 2012, reflecting both the scale of the storm damage and the company's commitment to restoring service as safely and quickly as possible. Additional mutual assistance crews continue to arrive and are being deployed to areas with the greatest remaining need. PPL Electric's advanced smart grid technology also helped reduce customer impacts during the storm. Automated equipment restored service or prevented outages for more than 60,000 customers, allowing crews to focus on repairing the most significant damage. Remaining Repairs Among Most Complex While outage numbers continue to decline, many of the remaining outages involve some of the most challenging repairs from this storm event. In several locations, crews are repairing multiple broken poles, extensive tree damage and significant sections of damaged electrical equipment before service can be safely restored. Many repairs require multiple work groups operating in sequence, including forestry personnel, damage assessors, line workers and other support teams. These repairs are labor-intensive and time-consuming but are necessary to safely rebuild damaged sections of the electric system. As restoration efforts progress, crews and equipment continue to be repositioned from substantially restored areas into the hardest-hit regions to get crews to where they are needed most and support customers who remain without service. Restoration Estimates Continue to Be Refined PPL Electric continues to refine restoration estimates as crews reach individual work locations and complete detailed field assessments. As crews continue to work through outages, customers may see estimated restoration times become more specific as on-site field crews assign targeted restoration times for individual outages. Customers are encouraged to monitor PPL Electric's outage map, mobile app and outage notifications for the latest information regarding their specific outage. Customer Support: Ice and Water Reimbursement PPL Electric recognizes the challenges customers face during extended outages, particularly during the summer. The company will reimburse customers, through a bill credit, for up to three gallons of water and three 10-pound bags of ice per day during the event. Customers seeking reimbursement should mail copies of itemized receipts, along with their account number, to: PPL Ice and Water Program, 827 Hausman Road, Allentown, PA 18104 . Customers do not need to call before submitting receipts. Stay Connected Report outages at pplelectric.com or by texting "Outage" to TXTPPL (898775). Download the free PPL Electric mobile app to report and track outages. Sign up for outage alerts at pplelectric.com/alerts . Check outage status and estimated restoration times at pplelectric.com/outage . Stay Safe Always assume downed wires are energized and stay far away from them. Report downed wires to PPL Electric or local emergency responders. Never operate a portable generator inside a home, garage or other enclosed area. Use flashlights instead of candles to reduce fire risk. Turn off appliances that were operating when power was lost. Make alternate arrangements if you or a family member relies on electricity for critical medical needs and call 9-1-1 if emergency assistance is required. Check on elderly relatives, neighbors and others who may need assistance. For the safety of both customers and crews, maintain a safe distance from all restoration work sites. For updates on storm restoration progress, visit pplelectric.com or download the PPL Electric Utilities mobile app. About PPL Electric Utilities PPL Electric Utilities delivers safe, reliable and affordable electricity to about 1.5 million homes and businesses in eastern and central Pennsylvania. It regularly ranks among the country’s best utility companies for reliability and customer satisfaction. PPL Electric Utilities is a major employer and an active supporter of the communities it serves. It is a part of the PPL Corporation (NYSE: PPL) family of companies. Visit pplelectric.com or connect on social media via Facebook , X and Instagram for energy efficiency tips, bill help information, guidance on shopping for an electricity supplier, storm updates and more.

title: The 7 biomarkers to read and track your chronic inflammation
summary: Chronic inflammation is often invisible. But it can be measured.
body_text: This listicle is inspired by our 2-part series on chronic inflammation: Part 1: Understanding the Causes → and Part 2: Levers for Action → . Low-grade chronic inflammation settles in quietly. No redness, no acute pain, just persistent fatigue, slower recovery, less restorative sleep. And yet, it is one of the mechanisms most involved in modern diseases: cardiovascular, metabolic, neurological, hormonal. The good news: it can be measured. Here are the 7 biomarkers to know in order to read your inflammatory terrain, identify priority levers, and check over time whether your lifestyle changes are actually producing an effect. 1. hsCRP: the reference marker for systemic inflammation High-sensitivity CRP is the most widely used protein to assess low-grade chronic inflammation. Why it matters : produced by the liver in response to systemic inflammation, hsCRP is now recommended to reassess cardiovascular risk. It is also sensitive to interventions on nutrition, exercise, and sleep, making it an excellent follow-up marker. Context : Persistent fatigue or slow recovery Non-restorative sleep Diffuse joint or muscle pain Easy abdominal weight gain Frequent infections Key takeaway : hsCRP is the first marker to request to objectify an inflammatory terrain. Always interpreted in context, never in isolation. 2. NLR: the ratio that reveals your immune balance The neutrophils-to-lymphocytes ratio is calculated from a simple blood count. Why it matters : this ratio reflects immune balance. An NLR above 3 is associated with systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. Interpretation must always be contextualized. Context : Frequent infections or immunity that seems less effective Persistent fatigue Difficult recovery Chronic stress Key takeaway : NLR is an inexpensive and valuable indicator to follow the evolution of the inflammatory terrain over time. 3. Ferritin: between iron status and inflammation Ferritin is an iron storage protein, but it is also an inflammation marker. Context : ferritin can rise in chronic inflammation, even without iron overload. An elevated ferritin must therefore always be read alongside other markers to distinguish iron excess from an inflammatory reaction. Warning signs : Unexplained fatigue Difficult recovery Known systemic inflammation Underlying inflammatory or liver condition Key takeaway : never read ferritin alone. Combined with hsCRP and a complete iron panel, it gives a fair reading of both iron status AND the inflammatory terrain. 4. Homocysteine: the metabolic and oxidative marker Homocysteine is an amino acid whose elevation reflects altered metabolism. Why it matters : its elevation often reflects a deficiency in B vitamins (B6, B9, B12) or oxidative stress. It is a marker associated with cardiovascular risk and metabolic dysfunction. Context : Chronic fatigue Brain fog, decreased concentration Mood instability, irritability, depressive tendency Family history of cardiovascular issues Key takeaway : homocysteine helps identify deficiencies in essential cofactors and oxidative stress. Often correctable through nutrition and targeted micronutrition. 5. ApoB / ApoA1: the cardiovascular ratio that goes beyond LDL Apolipoproteins reflect atherogenic particles (ApoB) and protective ones (ApoA1) respectively. Why it matters : the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio is a more precise indicator of cardiovascular risk than LDL alone. Oxidized LDL triggers an inflammatory cascade in the vascular wall and accelerates atherosclerosis. Context : Family history of cardiovascular issues Abdominal weight gain Unstable blood sugar Suspected oxidative stress Key takeaway : an unfavorable ApoB/ApoA1 ratio is a strong cardiovascular signal, even when classic LDL appears correct. 6. Omega 3/6 profile: the balance of essential fats The omega profile measures the balance between omega-3 and omega-6 in your body. Why it matters : a high omega-6/omega-3 ratio promotes a pro-inflammatory terrain. EPA and DHA are precursors of mediators involved in inflammation resolution. Context : Diet rich in processed products or oxidized oils Low intake of fatty fish Joint pain Difficult recovery Key takeaway : the omega profile is a lever that can be shifted quickly through nutrition (sardines, mackerel, herring, salmon, anchovies) or targeted supplementation. 7. Vitamin D: a foundation often insufficient Vitamin D acts like a hormone, regulating immunity, inflammation, and bone health. Why it matters : insufficiency is common. Recent large intervention studies suggest supplementation is most relevant in cases of documented insufficiency. In people with adequate status, benefits are less systematic. Context : Persistent fatigue with no clear cause Recurring infections Diffuse muscle or joint pain Low mood, loss of motivation Key takeaway : test before and during supplementation. Avoid blind high-dose supplementation. In summary: a terrain, not a single number These 7 biomarkers are not meant to be read in isolation. They make sense when placed in relation to one another, within a global reading of the terrain: metabolism, energy, hormones, recovery, nutrition, digestion, sleep, stress, physical activity, cardiovascular health. At Lucis, we analyze more than 110 biomarkers across 11 physiological systems. Our medical team interprets your results in context, identifies the priority levers for your terrain, and proposes a personalized plan.

title: Is memory the moat?
summary: The fastest open source LLMs for enterprise.
body_text: Over the past several months, we’ve seen an explosion in the capabilities of open source models. With DeepSeek V4-Pro and GLM5.2 reaching near-Opus levels of intelligence, open source has emerged as a real, cost-efficient alternative to the closed source models we’ve been married to. But we have yet to see one like Kimi K3. Promising Fable/Sol levels of intelligence, Kimi K3 marks the start of a new era for open source. But a smarter model means a bigger model — and these models are expanding in size just as fast as they are in capabilities. GLM5.2 has 753B parameters, DeepSeek V4-Pro 1.6T, and Kimi K3 weighs in at 2.8T (!!) parameters. That’s over 1.5TB of VRAM before allocating a KV cache for 1M tokens of context. Not even a B200 node (8 GPUs) can fit Kimi K3. That leaves you with limited options: serve on a node of B300s, which have 288GB of VRAM per GPU, or commit two B200 nodes (TP16) to serving Kimi. But guess which other non-NVIDIA GPU has 288GB of VRAM? AMD’s MI355X. Can you tell we like these chips yet? At around ~2.4× cheaper per GPU on average versus a B300 and ~1.7× cheaper than a B200, the MI355X is a cost-efficient alternative to Blackwells with comparable hardware specs. The only problem with AMD is software support — slower kernels and less day-0 support on inference frameworks make serving frontier models on AMD a real engineering effort. Our claim at Wafer is that agents are improving at kernel and model optimization, closing this gap as we speak. But with AMD shipping day-0 support for Kimi K3, most of the work was already done for us. The results are great: on a 1,024-token input / 400-token output benchmark, the MI355X reaches 952 tok/s/node and 118 tok/s single stream — over 3.8× the aggregate throughput per node and over 1.3× the single-stream decode of our TP16 B200 deployment (whose 498 tok/s is a 16-GPU, 2-node total — ~249/node). B300 nodes still win ~1.65× on aggregate throughput over the MI355X, but at 2.4× the price, the MI355X crushes the B300 on performance per dollar. 8× MI355X (TP8) 2×8 B200 (TP16) B300 (TP8+DCP8) Decode tok/s per stream 118 tok/s 90 tok/s 172 tok/s Peak aggregate 952 tok/s 498 tok/s 1,568 tok/s Peak aggregate per GPU 119 tok/s 31 tok/s 196 tok/s Peak aggregate per $/GPU-hr 48 tok/s/$ 7 tok/s/$ 33 tok/s/$ Perf/dollar at $2.50/GPU-hr for the MI355X, $6.00 for the B300, and $4.25 for the B200 . To the B200’s defence, its numbers are somewhat deflated by the fact that it pays a cross-node all-reduce on the decode critical path (RoCE v2 at ~195 Gb/s) — it’s the only config here that spans two nodes, because Kimi K3 won’t fit weights plus a 1M-token KV pool on a single 8×192GB node. But that’s exactly the point: Kimi K3 at its size is one of the first models we’ve seen where the MI355X’s focus on HBM capacity gives it a practical, measurable edge over the B200. How we did it While Kimi K3 served out of the box, there was still work to be done to get it to its current throughput number. The main lever was speculative decode. K3 ships zero draft tensors — no MTP, no EAGLE — so the only speculative path is an external block-diffusion draft: RadixArk’s Kimi-K3-DSpark . On CUDA it just runs. On ROCm our first real request breaks the scheduler with this error: NameError: name 'top_k_renorm_prob' is not defined. Did you mean: 'top_p_renorm_prob'? sglang’s accept-sampling verifier has two ways to build the target distribution: a dense path that calls top_k_renorm_prob , and a sparse fast path that routes through torch.topk directly. The CUDA build imports top_k_renorm_prob from sgl_kernel ; the ROCm build aliases only a Triton top-p kernel and leaves top_k_renorm_prob undefined — there’s no top-k renorm kernel for gfx950 to alias. So the moment a request lands on the dense path, the verifier hits that NameError and takes the scheduler down with it. The fix is a single PyTorch function. Top-k renorm is a small operation: take the model’s probability vector, keep the k highest entries, zero the rest, and rescale what’s left to sum to 1. A sort , a masked_fill , a divide — dropped straight into sglang’s ROCm sampling branch, the same computation the CUDA build gets from sgl_kernel . No custom kernel: the reflex on ROCm is to assume you need one, but here it was a missing definition, not a missing kernel. With spec dec fixed and hardened, we gained ~2.2× performance single-stream, ~1.7× per-stream at moderate load, and +18% peak aggregate. More importantly, our peak aggregate throughput landed on much higher concurrency (c64 vs c24 no-spec). Prefill optimizations Discussion around model performance tends to highlight decode tokens per second. But in many cases decode tok/s is fool’s gold — decode is over-glorified, while time-to-first-token, the number users feel the most, gets overlooked. The MI355X struggles here: an identical 172k-token cold prefill took ~51s on MI355X versus ~23s on a B300. On a 1M-context model, a lot of workloads have huge prefills (sometimes cold), and having GPUs spin on prefill for minutes can render entire fleets of nodes useless. The gap was almost entirely one kernel. K3 on ROCm was falling back to slow generic Triton attention because the fast AITER MLA prefill kernel wouldn’t load. The problem was a shape mismatch, not a missing kernel — K3 at TP8 gives 12 attention heads per rank, and AITER’s MLA path is built for 4, 8, or multiples of 16. The fix was trivially simple: zero-pad the head count 12→16, run the fast kernel, and extract the real 12 heads from the output. The result: on the same 172k cold prefill, the AITER MLA prefill ASM runs at ~13k tok/s steady-state vs the Triton fallback’s ~4–7k, speeding up prefill by ~2–3×. It’s a TTFT lever, not an aggregate-throughput one — decode is unchanged, so it doesn’t move the numbers above; it moves the number a user waits on before the first token appears. Takeaways Achieving the best performance-per-dollar ratio on the MI355X was relatively out of the box. There were some expected framework-related bugs — but fewer than GLM5.2 , and this time it certainly did not require custom kernels . SOTA on AMD is imminent. Is the CUDA moat dead?

title: How Mercari boosted seller confidence and drove millions more listings with Photoroom
summary: Discover how Mercari helps casual sellers list with confidence - anywhere, anytime - using Photoroom’s background editing
body_text: Life before Photoroom Sellers struggled with listing due to messy or private backgrounds Casual sellers hesitant to photograph items in cluttered spaces iOS SDK and other third-party tools delivered poor quality product images Many listings abandoned, reducing marketplace supply Life with Photoroom Simple automated background blur button increases seller confidence Millions of photos processed monthly with seamless API integration Increased number of listings by casual sellers and heavy users Projected 10% adoption, targeting 1% increase in marketplace listings (massive impact for Japan's dominant C2C marketplace) Nick Pittoni has seen marketplace behaviors across continents—from the UK to Germany, Spain to the US. But nothing prepared him for the unspoken rules of selling in Japan. As Product Lead for AI and LLM consumer applications at Mercari, Japan's dominant C2C marketplace, Nick discovered that Japanese sellers operate by a completely different playbook. "There's a high bar for sellers and buyers, and you're kind of expected to know what you're doing," he explains. "Otherwise you get penalized. You can get negative feedback fairly easily." This cultural expectation creates a unique challenge: in a country where most of the population knows Mercari and many have accounts, the pressure to create perfect listings can actually prevent people from selling at all. And for a marketplace that thrives on fresh inventory, hesitant sellers translate directly to missed revenue opportunities. When perfect becomes the enemy of good enough Japan's marketplace culture demands authenticity at a level that would surprise most Western sellers. Japanese sellers meticulously document every scratch, stain, and imperfection with detailed photos and descriptions. “If you're buying a CD or a game, they would photograph the back at precisely the right angle to show buyers exactly how many scratches to expect,” shares Nick. But this commitment to transparency created an unexpected bottleneck. Through regular user interviews, Nick's team discovered that several sellers were listing less frequently not because of the items themselves, but because of where they were taking the photos. "Many sellers are often very conscious about where they're taking their photos. In Japan, more often than not, maybe the house is a bit small, the space is kind of cramped, and the background can be messy." — Nick Pittoni, AI/LLM Consumer Product Lead at Mercari The result? Potential sellers would postpone or abandon their listings entirely rather than show a messy room or reveal their private spaces. For Mercari, this meant reduced marketplace liquidity and missed growth opportunities. Nick had tried various solutions before, including a previous collaboration with Photoroom during its infancy. In recent years, his team explored iOS SDK tools, third-party models, and other AI tools, focusing on buyer experience and conversion. But as Nick would realize, “The quality wasn't very good across the board, and we didn't see the conversion improve.” It became clear to Nick that they needed a solution that delivered accurate results and solved the real pains of sellers. A single-button solution for sellers When Nick's team reconnected with Photoroom years later, the technology had evolved significantly. More importantly, they’d learned to focus on the right problem: seller confidence rather than buyer conversion. Integration with the Photoroom background removal API was simple. Implementation timeline: A small team of 3-4 engineers at Mercari brought the feature from initial discussion to production in 2-3 months. Solution focus: They prioritized the background blur feature to remove distractions from product photos while retaining the real life appearance of the product. Sellers new process: When Mercari sellers open the live camera to photograph an item, they click a single button and it instantly blurs their background. "The Photoroom API was very easy to integrate with. Working with the Photoroom commercial and technical teams was smooth and straightforward, we got to production quickly with a small team.” — Nick Pittoni, AI/LLM Consumer Product Lead at Mercari What impressed Nick most wasn't just the quality, but the scale Photoroom could handle. Mercari is a complex marketplace with billions of listings. Having Photoroom’s infrastructure on their side makes it easy to process millions of images, freeing their engineering team to focus on more strategic projects. “Photoroom processes high single digit million images monthly for our sellers without slowing the listing experience.” — Nick Pittoni, AI/LLM Consumer Product Lead at Mercari The expected and surprising results The impact became clear almost immediately after launching the background blur feature. Increased number of listings Photoroom's background blur solved a distinctly human problem: the anxiety of sharing private spaces. By removing a psychological barrier that was preventing listings, Mercari unlocked millions of additional photos and measurably increased marketplace supply. ”After launching the ability to blur listings’ backgrounds, there was very significant boost in average number of items published by casual sellers, and a positive impact across all segments” — Nick Pittoni, AI/LLM Consumer Product Lead at Mercari Expansive seller adoption More intriguingly, the feature attracted unexpected users. While Nick's team hypothesized that casual, light sellers would be the primary adopters, "pro sellers or heavy sellers are adopting this feature a lot more than the light sellers," Nick shares. These experienced sellers, who presumably already had their own photo editing workflows, embraced the convenience of in-app background removal. Ambitious adoption rate Mercari is targeting more seller adoption of the background blur feature, which they estimate will increase overall marketplace listings by 1%. “We can share indicatively that with an adoption rate of 10% of users, we are aiming to raise the amount of listings on the marketplace by 1%.” — Nick Pittoni, AI/LLM Consumer Product Lead at Mercari For a startup, 1% might sound modest. But for a C2C environment at Mercari's scale, that translates to enormous business impact on GMV and revenue. Improved sellers’ confidence The feature means sellers can avoid worrying about where they list from. Oftentimes in Japan, young people may help older parents get rid of unwanted objects, but taking photos can be challenging in such locations. Whether it's the clutter or the old school looking floor, now they don't have to worry about it. “Photoroom helps sellers build confidence to showcase the products they’re most passionate about. By boosting sellers' confidence when taking listing photos, anyone can list anything, anywhere, at any time.” — Nick Pittoni, AI/LLM Consumer Product Lead at Mercari Looking ahead While focused on maximizing adoption of the background blur feature, Nick's team continues exploring Photoroom as a visual partner. "We are always exploring and staying in touch with the Photoroom team, learning about all the new features and testing them out. We tried one of the latest features recently to improve the lighting." — Nick Pittoni, AI/LLM Consumer Product Lead at Mercari The key, Nick emphasizes, is staying grounded in real sellers’ problems rather than getting swept up in AI capabilities, echoing a shared value with the Photoroom team. "With AI it's very easy to get excited and create new problems that maybe users don't have and bloat your product experience,” says Nick. “So sometimes it's just the simple things that make the overall experience better."

title: 12 Long-Distance Relationship Movies to Watch Together In Sync Online
summary: Take a look through our favorite movies for long-distance relationships to watch in sync online for your next virtual date!
body_text: There’s nothing quite as romantic as the notion of love so powerful that it can withstand the test of distance and time. That kind of love takes nurturing, devotion, and patience. One of the best ways you can stay connected to your long-distance partner and keep the spark alive is by having virtual date nights — and what better date than a movie that relates to your own situation? Here are 12 long-distance love stories we recommend that you watch with your long-distance partner to give you both the hope and encouragement you need. They’re sure to bring the two of you closer together despite your physical separation. Going the Distance If you loved 50 First Dates or The Wedding Singer, you’re bound to love Going the Distance . Starring Drew Barrymore, this is the story of two career-driven people who weren’t looking for a relationship. What started as a casual hookup turns into a long-distance romance and tells the story of how the couple is able to keep their love alive while leading separate lives in different places of the world. One Day Anne Hathaway brings a reassuring familiarity and sense of character to her films. One Day follows Emma and Dexter — two friends from college who reunite once each year for 20 years to celebrate the day they met. The movie tells a beautiful story that underscores the importance of friendship in an enduring love and points out how often we lose sight of the happiness that’s right under our noses. Like Crazy Like Crazy is about a pair of love-struck students, Anna and Jacob. The two are suddenly and tragically torn apart by the terms of a visa, which sends Anna back home to London. The couple finds that, no matter what earthly forces try to drive them apart, they always manage to find their way back to each other. Dear John Novelist and screenwriter Nicholas Sparks has a way with love stories. Dreamy Channing Tatum and darling Amanda Seyfried star in this tear-jerking chick flick. Savannah and John’s relationship is tested when John, a soldier in the army, is deployed after the terrorist attacks of September 11th, 2001. The two keep in touch via letters, but letters can only keep their relationship afloat for so long. Sleepless in Seattle Imagine falling in love with someone you heard on the radio. That’s exactly what happens to Annie (played by Meg Ryan) in the 1993 favorite Sleepless in Seattle when she hears Sam (played by Tom Hanks) talk about his relatable feelings on a late-night talk radio program. Find out how these two strangers make their way to each other in the bustling city of Seattle. The Notebook The best relationships are the ones that overcome the odds that seem to be stacked against them. This is the case for Noah and Allie, portrayed by Ryan Gosling and Rachel McAdams. Noah is called to serve in the military in World War II, but this is far from where their relationship ends. Years later, the two find each other again, but Allie is engaged. Will they find their way back to each other? Watch The Notebook , another riveting Nicholas Sparks romance, to find out. You’ve Got Mail Meeting online isn’t all that unusual these days, but in the 1990s, it certainly wasn’t the norm. Another Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan smash, You’ve Got Mail is about two booksellers who fall in love online only to realize they are rivals in real life. How will they manage to reconcile their disdain for each other with the feelings they’ve developed through their emails? The Time Traveler’s Wife Romance and science fiction collide in the best of ways in The Time Traveler’s Wife . Henry and Clare are deeply in love, but Henry’s genetic disorder causes him to involuntarily travel through time. This creates complications in his relationship with his wife — and their ability to have children. Will a series of sporadic visits be enough to sustain their relationship? The Other End of the Line In The Other End of the Line , Priya, an Indian call center agent, falls in love with Granger, an American playboy, over the phone while working. He eventually invites her out to San Francisco where they have a whirlwind romance. All isn’t as easy as it seems, though, as they must overcome cultural differences and familial disapproval. Find out if they’re able to successfully merge their worlds and make their love work. A Very Long Engagement If you had reason to believe your true love may have survived a deadly event despite being reported dead, how far would you go to look for them? Based on a novel, A Very Long Engagement follows Mathilde as she searches France for her fiance after World War I. The Lake House What if the person you loved was living two years apart from you? Icons Keanu Reeves and Sandra Bullock play a lonely doctor and an architect who fall in love through letters while inhabiting the same lake house several years apart from each other. How is this possible? And will they ever meet? Watch The Lake House to find out. Try Hyperbeam Together Today Couples often still have a lot of long-distance love movies to catch up on together. title: Keurig Now Offers Café-Quality Cold Brew on Tap
summary: The new dual-tap system delivers café-quality cold brew and nitro in seconds—unlocking a simpler, scalable way to meet growing demand for cold coffee Cold coffee is reshaping beverage menus across foodservice, as younger consumers and beverage-led concepts drive demand well beyond the morning daypart. To help operators keep pace, Keurig Dr Pepper is launching the […]
body_text: The new dual-tap system delivers café-quality cold brew and nitro in seconds—unlocking a simpler, scalable way to meet growing demand for cold coffee Cold coffee is reshaping beverage menus across foodservice, as younger consumers and beverage-led concepts drive demand well beyond the morning daypart. To help operators keep pace, Keurig Dr Pepper is launching the Keurig® K-Tap Nitro & Cold Beverage Dispenser —a new innovation designed to bring premium nitro and cold coffee on tap to high-traffic, away-from-home environments. Now commercially available following successful demos and operator trials, the K‑Tap system enables workplaces, quick-service restaurants, convenience stores and other venues—from movie theaters to sports and concert arenas—to serve both still and nitro cold brew in seconds. Built for How Consumers Drink Coffee Today Cold brew has quickly become a staple across foodservice channels, fueled by Gen Z and Millennial consumers. “Cold coffee remains a top choice for Gen Z and Millennials, and some of the fastest-growing QSR chains are advertising programs that lead with cold coffee beverages,” said Jennifer Garczyk, Vice President & General Manager, Away From Home at Keurig Dr Pepper. “With the K‑Tap system, we’re giving our partners a simple, reliable way to deliver premium cold coffee experiences that meet that demand—no matter the setting.” Café‑Quality, Without the Complexity While demand for cold brew and nitro continues to grow, traditional systems can be complex to install and operate. The K‑Tap system is designed to change that—this compact, countertop unit delivers a high-quality experience in a more streamlined, operator-friendly format. The system uses patented, flash chill technology to cool beverages to 35°F and pours both classic cold brew and smooth, velvety nitro at the touch of a tap. With no need for nitrogen tanks, additional consumables or complex plumbing, the K‑Tap system simplifies operations without sacrificing quality. Paired with REVV® Coffee Concentrate, each pour delivers a smooth, balanced profile with notes of citrus, figs, molasses and chocolate— helping operators serve the growing cold coffee occasion with speed, simplicity and café-style consistency.

body_text: When it comes to B2B payments, inefficiencies are not just a hindrance; they are a costly liability. A 2024 PYMNTS survey revealed that 80% of executives admitted to losing money and business due to the inefficiencies in their payment processes. Yet, many businesses continue to rely on outdated, manual systems. If you're still dealing with paper checks and chasing approvals, it's time for a reality check. You are lagging behind your competition and overlooking one of the most powerful tools available to modern businesses today: B2B payment automation . The truth is that by automating your B2B payment processes, you can transform time-consuming tasks into seamless, error-free operations. This shift can enable your company to make faster payments, boost financial visibility, and improve vendor relationships. In this comprehensive guide, we’ll explore how B2B payment automation works, why it’s no longer optional, its benefits, and how it can revolutionise your business's financial operations. What is B2B Payment Automation? B2B payment automation refers to the use of technology to automate the processes involved in sending and receiving payments between businesses. Instead of relying on manual processes, such as checks or manual invoice entries, payment automation allows for seamless and fast electronic transfers integrated with your business operations. Automation ensures that payments are processed more quickly and with fewer errors, freeing up valuable time for your team and reducing the likelihood of missed payments or delays. In essence, B2B payment automation empowers your business to manage its finances more effectively, foster stronger supplier partnerships, and position itself for scalable growth. Types of B2B Payment Methods Businesses now have a range of options for B2B transactions. Your chosen method can significantly impact your operational efficiency, cash flow, and overall business relationships. Here are some of the most common B2B payment methods you can choose from: Traditional Methods These methods rely on time-tested processes that require more manual oversight and can often slow down transactions. Paper Checks : These remain prevalent in B2B transactions due to their familiarity and simplicity. However, they’re riddled with challenges like slower processing times and increased fraud susceptibility. Wire Transfers : A great way to securely and swiftly transfer funds directly between banks, particularly in international transactions, are wire transfers. However, they incur higher fees and require additional administrative oversight. Automated Clearing House (ACH) Payments : ACH payments facilitate the electronic transfer of funds between banks and are commonly used for recurring payments and domestic transactions. Digital Options Fast, secure, and easily integrated into existing systems, these methods leverage technology to enable smooth, real-time transactions. Credit and Debit Cards : These are perhaps the most widely accepted in B2B transactions since they offer convenience and immediate processing and are particularly useful for smaller transactions and online purchases. Virtual Cards : Providing enhanced security by generating unique card numbers for each transaction, virtual cards are ideal for managing vendor payments and controlling spending. Digital Payment Platforms : Platforms like PayPal, Google Pay, and Stripe facilitate seamless online transactions and support various payment methods, including credit cards and bank transfers. Emerging Payment Options New-age solutions are challenging conventional systems by offering faster, more decentralized ways to transfer funds across borders. Cryptocurrencies : Payment methods, such as Bitcoin and Ethereum, are gaining traction in B2B transactions due to their potential for lower transaction fees and faster cross-border payments. Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Payment Systems : These P2P payment systems enable businesses to transfer funds directly to each other without intermediaries, offering convenience and speed. Evaluating these payment options against your business needs can help you make an informed decision that boosts your business efficiency. While selecting the right payment method is crucial, it’s equally crucial to explore how B2B payment automation can take your business operations to the next level. Benefits of B2B Payment Automation As your business continues to grow and scale, understanding the impact of B2B payment automation is crucial. After all, embracing automation that simplifies and optimises payment processes is the best way to stay ahead of the competition. Thus, recognising the benefits of automation can help you achieve more effective financial operations. Let's explore the specific benefits that B2B payment automation brings to the table. Lower Administrative Costs Manual payment processes are resource-intensive, involving substantial time and labour. Automation eliminates costly errors and reduces the need for manual data entry and paperwork, leading to significant cost savings. In fact, studies indicate that automated, digital payments are nearly 14 times more cost-effective than traditional payment methods. Enhanced Efficiency and Faster Payment Processing B2B payment automation accelerates payment cycles by eliminating delays caused by manual data entry and approval steps. This reduces the time spent on each transaction, leading to quicker invoice processing and faster payment execution. Automation also frees up your employees to focus on high-value tasks, improving operational efficiency. Reduced Errors and Increased Accuracy Automated payment systems minimise human intervention, thereby decreasing the likelihood of errors such as duplicate payments or incorrect amounts. This leads to more accurate financial records, especially on a large scale. Accurate payments also reduce the number of disputes with vendors, ensuring smoother financial operations for you. Better Financial Visibility and Cash Flow Management B2B payment automation provides real-time tracking and insights into payment processes, offering you up-to-date insights into your financial status. With automated systems, your company can monitor cash flow more effectively, make informed decisions on spending, and maintain better control over its financial health. This visibility also aids strategic financial planning. Strengthened Vendor Relationships Through Timely Payments Automated payments ensure all transactions are consistently processed on time, which builds trust with vendors. Timely payments enhance reliability and enable smooth collaboration between suppliers and your business. By reducing delays and errors, you can strengthen vendor relationships and gain access to better payment terms and discounts. Improved Security and Fraud Prevention Automated payment systems incorporate advanced security measures like encryption and multi-factor authentication to protect against fraud. These features safeguard sensitive financial data and reduce the risk of unauthorised transactions. They also eliminate human errors, which can lead to security breaches or fraud, ensuring safe and secure transactions. High Scalability B2B payment automation solutions are designed to scale with your growing business. As transaction volumes increase, the system can efficiently handle higher workloads without a corresponding rise in administrative costs. This scalability ensures your business can maintain operational efficiency even as your needs expand, enabling future growth. Simplified Compliance and Audit Automated payment systems provide comprehensive transaction records that streamline the auditing process. By maintaining detailed logs of all payments and invoices, your business can easily comply with financial regulations. This reduces the complexity of audits and ensures you remain on track with legal requirements and industry standards. Ready to transform your financial operations? Get started with Kodo today and experience the benefits of streamlined B2B payment automation. Key Components of B2B Payment Automation Solutions With payment automation no longer being just a convenience, your business must look towards robust solutions to simplify your financial operations. But do you know how these solutions actually achieve this? Every solution has some integral components that streamline the automation process, and you need to be aware of them. Automated Invoice Processing : B2B payment solutions use technologies like Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to extract data from invoices, eliminating manual data entry. They can match invoices to purchase orders, accelerating the invoicing cycle, reducing errors, and ensuring invoices are processed promptly. Payment Approval Workflows : Another key component of any automation solution is payment approval workflows . These workflows ensure that each payment is reviewed and approved by the relevant parties only in accordance with your company's approval process. This speeds up the approval process and enforces compliance with internal controls. Payment Execution Integration with Multiple Payment Methods : A robust solution integrates various payment methods such as ACH, credit cards, and wire transfers into a unified platform, allowing you to execute payments efficiently. This provides your business with the flexibility to select the most cost-effective payment method for each transaction. Reconciliation and Reporting Automation : B2B payment solutions have automated reconciliation tools that match payments with corresponding invoices and bank statements, identifying discrepancies in real time. This reduces manual effort, enhances accuracy, and provides your finance teams with up-to-date financial reports, facilitating better decision-making. Compliance and Security Features : B2B payment automation solutions incorporate robust security measures, including encryption and fraud detection, to protect sensitive financial data. This ensures all payments are secure and comply with proper financial regulations and legal standards. How to Implement B2B Payment Automation Solutions? Implementing a robust B2B payment automation solution requires careful planning and strategic decision-making. From assessing your current processes to selecting the right automation solution, the process involves several key steps that ensure the system fits seamlessly into your existing financial ecosystem. Here’s the detailed step-by-step process of implementing a B2B payment automation solution in your organisation. Step 1: Assess Current Processes and Vendor Payment Systems Before implementing a B2B payment automation solution, it’s important to thoroughly assess your existing payment workflows. Identify bottlenecks, manual interventions, and areas prone to errors. This is crucial for selecting the right automation solution. This assessment will become the foundation for a tailored automation strategy that addresses your business's specific needs. Step 2: Define Goals and Select Appropriate Automation Solution Vendor Once you’ve assessed your needs, clearly articulate the objectives you aim to achieve with automation, such as reducing processing time, minimising errors, or enhancing compliance. This will guide you in selecting a vendor that offers a solution that aligns with your objectives. You’ll also need to consider factors such as cost, scalability, integration capabilities, and support. Step 3: Develop an Implementation Plan and Train the Team Next, create a detailed implementation roadmap outlining timelines, responsibilities, and milestones to ensure the automation solution integrates smoothly into your business. Simultaneously, develop a comprehensive training programmme for your team to make sure they become proficient in using the new system. Step 4: Monitor Performance and Continuously Optimise Post-implementation, establish key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure the effectiveness of your automation solution. Regularly review these metrics to identify areas for improvement. Engage with your team to gather feedback and make necessary adjustments to workflows. Payment automation is not a set-and-forget solution, and ongoing optimisation will ensure it delivers maximum value. With this solid process in place, you’ll be able to implement an automation solution correctly to reimagine your financial workflows and enhance efficiency and accuracy. What are Some Top Considerations for a Scalable B2B Payment Automation Solution? When implementing B2B payment automation, choosing a solution that meets your current needs and scales as your business grows is essential. For this, you need to evaluate a few key factors carefully to ensure your chosen automation solution supports your long-term financial goals. Flexibility : Your B2B payment solution should support multiple payment methods and offer a centralised, secure platform to administer them. It must also support international payments. Integration Capabilities : Your solution must also be able to seamlessly integrate with your existing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems, accounting software, and banking platforms. This is crucial to ensuring all your transactions, approvals, and payments are in complete sync. Advanced Reporting : Your chosen solution must have robust reporting tools to enable real-time visibility into cash flow, payment statuses, and financial metrics, empowering you to make well-informed decisions and strategic plans. Ease of Use : Your solution must also have an intuitive user interface and straightforward workflows. This ensures quick adoption by your team, reduces training time, and enhances operational efficiency. Scalability and Cost : The solution should be capable of handling increasing transaction volumes without compromising performance. It must also offer a cost-effective approach to accommodate your business growth. Customer Service : The vendor of your selected solution must offer responsive and knowledgeable customer support to address your issues promptly and ensure the smooth operation of your payment processes. Conclusion The world of B2B payment automation is evolving, transforming how your business manages its financial processes.
